9.1.2. qnav.earth.dted

9.1.2.1. dted.py

summary:

A module for managing Digital Terrain Elevation Data (DTED). This is responsible for the reading and dynamic loading of DTED files for extracting and interpolating elevation from a locally stored Digital Elevation Map (DEM). This allows the extraction of the terrain height above the WSG84 ellipsoid, excluding man-made features. This is namely used for waypoint/trajectory generation of man-made features.

authors:
Michael Wright - mjwright@liverpool.ac.uk
version:

1.0.0 - First full implementation of this module.

class qnav.earth.dted.DtedTile(origin_lat: int, origin_lon: int, dted_dir: Path, dted_version: int = 2, interp_method: str = 'linear', is_empty_on_error: bool = True)[source]

Holds and handles the read content for a single DTED file. Manages the data contained in a DTED tile (1-degree by 1-degree region). This allows local interpolation and other relevant calculations. Instances of this are used by DtedHandler for dynamic loading and management of terrain information.

get_elevation(lat: float, lon: float, method: str = None) → float[source]

Interpolates the terrain elevation for the requested position. Given a latitude and longitude, the interpolated terrain elevation will be return (in metres). Optionally, an overriding interpolation method to use can be provided.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate of the reference position.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate of the reference position.

  • method (str) –

    An alternative interpolation method to use. Supported values are: ‘linear’, ‘nearest’, ‘slinear’, ‘cubic’,

    ’quintic’ and ‘pchip’.

Returns:

The interpolated terrain elevation (in metres)

Return type:

float

is_position_covered(lat: float, lon: float) → bool[source]

A method for checking if a requested point is covered by the tile. Performs a check to see if the position is encompassed by the tile, allowing its terrain heights to be interpolated.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate of the reference position.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate of the reference position.

Returns:

True if the point is covered by the tile.

Return type:

bool

A vectorised method for checking if points are covered by the tile. Performs a check to see which positions are encompassed by the tile, supporting their terrain heights to be interpolated.

Parameters:

  • lat (npt.ArrayLike) – The latitude coordinates of the reference positions.

  • lon (npt.ArrayLike) – The longitude coordinates of the reference positions.

Returns:

A boolean array indicating which points are covered by the tile. True is used for points inside the tile.

Return type:

np.ndarray.

distance_to_centre(lat: float, lon: float) → float[source]

Returns approximation to distance from centre of tile (in metres). Calculates the approximate to distance from centre of tile for the given position. Namely used to identify the most distant tile.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinate of the reference position.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinate of the reference position.

Returns:

The distance from the centre of the tile (in metres).

Return type:

float

class qnav.earth.dted.DtedHandler(dted_dir: Path, dted_version: int = 2, max_tiles: int = None, method: str = None)[source]

Manages the dynamic loading and handling of regions of DTED data. This class is use dynamically load DTED data for extracting elevation. This automatically determines the required DTED files and loads into memory. Constraints on the maximum amount of data to load can be set to conserve resources.

get_elevation(lat: float, lon: float, method: str = None) → float[source]

Interpolates the terrain elevation for the requested position. Performed interpolation of the terrain elevation for the given latitude and longitude location. Optionally an overriding interpolation method can be used.

Parameters:

  • lat (float) – The latitude coordinates of the reference positions.

  • lon (float) – The longitude coordinates of the reference positions.

  • method (str) – The overriding interpolation method to use. Supported methods are: ‘linear’, ‘nearest’, ‘slinear’, ‘cubic’, ‘quintic’ and ‘pchip’.

Returns:

The interpolated terrain elevation (in metres).

Return type:

float

get_elevation_vec(lat_points: ndarray, lon_points: ndarray, method: str = None) → ndarray[source]

Interpolates the terrain elevation at given positions. Performed vectorised interpolation of the terrain elevation for the given latitude and longitude locations. Optionally an overriding

interpolation method can be used.

Parameters:

  • lat_points (np.ndarray) – The latitude coordinates of the reference positions.

  • lon_points (np.ndarray) – The longitude coordinates of the reference positions.

  • method (str) – The overriding interpolation method to use. Supported methods are: ‘linear’, ‘nearest’, ‘slinear’, ‘cubic’, ‘quintic’ and ‘pchip’.

Returns:

The interpolated terrain elevation (in metres).

Return type:

np.ndarray

set_max_tiles(value: int)[source]

A setter method for the maximum number of tiles. Can use the value None to remove limit on number of tiles to hold.

Parameters:

value (int) – The maximum number of DTED tiles to hold in the cache.

clear_cache()[source]

Clears all cached DTED from memory. Simply removes all DTED tiles from the cache.

qnav.earth.dted.get_dted_file_path(dted_dir: Path, origin_lat: int, origin_lon: int, dted_version: int) → Path[source]

Give a latitude, longitude and optional DTED version number, this function generates the file path of the DTED file that would contain information for the given position.

Parameters:

  • dted_dir (Path) – The parent database_dir of the DTED files.

  • origin_lat (int) – The integer latitude value (south-most coordinate).

  • origin_lon (int) – The integer longitude value (west-most coordinate).

  • dted_version (int) – The version of the DTED data.

:return the location of a corresponding DTED file. :rtype: Path

qnav.earth.dted.read_dted_file(file_dir: Path) → dict[source]

Extracts elevation information from a provided DTED file (in metres). When provided with the location of a DTED file (of any level), this function will return an elevation matrix and latitude-longitude spacing of each point. This function reads DTED files of format version 1.1.

Parameters:

file_dir (Path) – The location of the DTED file to be read.

Returns:

A dictionary containing the contents of the DTED file. This contains the extracted origin coordinates, step sizes, coordinate ticks and elevation matrix.

Return type:

dict

qnav.earth.dted.get_template_dted_data(origin_lat: int, origin_lon: int, num_lat_points: int = 2, num_lon_points: int = 2) → dict[source]

Generates a template DTED data dictionary as if read from a file. Simulates the output of read_dted_file() by generating identical output structure with flat elevation. This is to be used as substitution for missing/unavailable DTED files.

Parameters:

  • origin_lat (int) – The integer latitude value (south-most coordinate).

  • origin_lon (int) – The integer longitude value (west-most coordinate).

  • num_lat_points (int) – The number of latitude points (rows) to generate.

  • num_lon_points (int) – The number of longitude points (columns) to generate.

Returns:

A dictionary containing contents of a DTED file. This contains the imitated origin coordinates, step sizes, coordinate ticks and elevation matrix that would be read.

Return type:

dict
